how: One source mutation applied to the working tree, the named gate run against it, then the file restored before the next row (`before` is the shipped source the row was run against, `after` the text that replaced it). Round 1's rows ran on lease G28-fn0rg and fix round 1's on G28-n0naq, both pair-a (`iPhone 17` / iOS 27 and emulator-5574 / API 35, Metro 8295). Filtered gate names satisfy nothing but their own name. Each row's tree digest is the `trees.android` half the run was keyed to, so a run can be matched to the build it pressed.

mutations.mutation: the row stops honouring `enabled`, and the model stops checking it either, so a disabled action is an ordinary row
mutations.second_hunk: the same row, in DialogModel.performAction: `if (action.disabled) {\n      return\n    }` deleted, so nothing else in the component refuses the press either
redTests: takes no tap on a disabled action, and draws it disabled (alert): expected 'locked:action:locked,locked:presented…' to be ''
takes no tap on a disabled action, and draws it disabled (confirmation): expected '1,1,1' to be '1,0,1'
reports the sheet rows as the component draws them, disabled included: expected 'Locked,Go,Wipe' to be 'Locked~,Go,Wipe'
mutations.note: One mutation, three red lines - and fix round 1's last row is what says which of them belong to which layer: `drawn=1,0,1` and the `~` in the dump are the row's own state, while the alert's event log went red because the deleted guard was the last thing standing between a disabled alert button and `onAction`. Both hunks were off here, so no line in this row isolates the row from the model.

mutations.mutation: the same one as the row above: `enabled = !action.disabled` becomes `enabled = true` and the guard leaves `DialogModel.performAction` - two hunks, so this row shows what a finger does when *nothing* refuses the press, not which layer refuses it alone
redTests: the sheet's disabled row is not enabled — expected false, saw true
a real tap on the disabled row leaves the sheet up — expected 1, saw 0
and reports nothing: the log gained only Back's close — expected …action:ok > presented:false > presented:false, saw …action:ok > presented:false > action:locked-row > presented:false
the real tap on "Copy link": 3 real taps left dialog-log "…action:locked-row > presented:false > action:copy > presented:false" rather than "…presented:false > action:copy > presented:false"
mutations.note: A real finger, not a dump - but read it with fix round 1's caveat: the guard was deleted here too, so lines 2 and 3 (the sheet came down, and the log gained `action:locked-row`) are what happens with *both* layers off, and only line 1 (`the sheet's disabled row is not enabled`) is the row's own state. Fix round 1's last row is the one that isolates the row. An earlier run of this mutation (08-55-46Z) went red on the first line and then aborted, because the check read the log text while the sheet's own window owned the dump - fixed in 17eb1958 before this row, and the fix is what let lines 2-4 be seen at all.
